gp.text: The following table provides sales, gross profit and operating income by reporting segment:

oi.text: In 2025, Innospec delivered a mixed set of results with continued strong operating income growth and margin expansion in Fuel Specialties offsetting lower results in Performance Chemicals and Oilfield Services.

opex.text: Operating expenses: decreased by $4.5 million year over year, primarily due to lower provisions for performance-related remuneration accruals, together with lower charges for doubtful debts.

costs.text: Operating expenses: decreased by $4.5 million year over year, primarily due to lower provisions for performance-related remuneration accruals, together with lower charges for doubtful debts.

rd.text: Operating expenses: the year over year decrease of $2.9 million was due to lower provisions for performance-related remuneration accruals, lower research and development expenditure and favorable movements for doubtful debt provisions.

nonop.heading: Other Income Statement Captions
nonop.text:
Corporate costs: the year over year increase of $2.6 million was due to the prior year including the recovery of $8.4 million of historical pension costs, increased provisions for asset retirement obligations in relation to our legacy operations, the additional investment in our IT infrastructure and the amortization of the group's new ERP system, being partly offset by lower provisions for performance-related remuneration accruals.

Adjustment to fair value of contingent consideration: the credit in the current year of $15.9 million compares to an expense of $3.4 million in the prior year. The amounts in both years relate to the acquisition of QGP Química Geral (“QGP”) within our Performance Chemicals segment. See Note 14 of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information.

Restructuring charge: the charge in the current year is $0.9 million compared to no charge in the prior year. The charge relates to our operations in South America within our Performance Chemicals segment.

Impairment of property, plant and equipment: the charge in the current year is $22.9 million compared to no charge in the prior year. The charge relates to our Oilfield Services segment.

tax.text: Income taxes: The effective tax rate was 15.6% and 13.6% in 2025 and 2024, respectively. The adjusted effective tax rate, as calculated by adjusting income before taxes and by adjusting income taxes for the items set out in the following table, was 24.1% in 2025 compared with 26.4% in 2024. The Company believes this adjusted effective tax rate, a non-GAAP financial measure, provides useful information to investors and may assist them in evaluating the Company’s underlying performance and identifying operating trends. In addition, management uses this non-GAAP financial measure internally to evaluate the performance of the Company’s operations and for planning and forecasting in subsequent periods.

ocf.heading: Operating activities
ocf.text:
Operating lease commitments relate primarily to right-of-use assets at third-party manufacturing facilities, office space, motor vehicles and various items of computer and office equipment which are expected to be renewed and replaced in the normal course of business.

The interest payments on debt are the commitment fees for our $250.0 million revolving credit facility. Any interest income has been excluded.

wc.heading: Working Capital
wc.text:
In 2025 our working capital increased by $59.3 million, while our adjusted working capital increased by $33.9 million. The difference between the net movement for current assets and current liabilities and the adjusted working capital measure shown in the table below, is primarily due to the movements for income taxes.

The Company believes that adjusted working capital, a non-GAAP financial measure, provides useful information to investors in evaluating the Company’s underlying performance and identifying operating trends. Management uses this non-GAAP financial measure internally to allocate resources and evaluate the performance of the Company’s operations. Items excluded from the adjusted working capital calculation are listed in the table below and represent factors which do not fluctuate in line with the day to day working capital needs of the business.

The movements in our adjusted working capital are explained as follows:

We had an $0.6 million increase in trade and other accounts receivable due to the timing of sales across our reporting segments and the mix of customer payment terms.

capex.text: For the full year, cash from operations after capital expenditures remained strong at $63.9 million. As of December 31, 2025, Innospec had $292.5 million in cash and cash equivalents and no debt. Full year dividend payments increased by 10 percent over the prior year to $1.71 per share and we bought back 264 thousand shares at a cost of $23.9 million. We continue to have significant balance sheet flexibility for M&A, dividend growth, organic investment and buybacks.

intro.text: When we use the terms “Innospec,” “the Corporation,” “the Company,” “Registrant,” “we,” “us” and “our,” we are referring to Innospec Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries unless otherwise indicated or the context otherwise requires. Innospec develops, manufactures, blends, markets and supplies a wide range of specialty chemicals to customers in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific. Our Performance Chemicals business creates innovative technology-based solutions for the personal care, home care, agrochemical, construction, mining and other industrial markets. Our Fuel Specialties business specializes in manufacturing and supplying fuel additives that improve fuel efficiency, boost engine performance and reduce harmful emissions.

oi.text: In Fuel Specialties, revenues were up 1 percent and operating income increased 18 percent. Operating margin improved to just below our target of 19 to 21 percent. We remain focused on further margin improvement in parallel with topline growth. With our industry-leading innovation and customer service capabilities, we are well positioned to continue advancing our global customers’ initiatives. Our technology will continue to focus on cleaner fuels, lowering emissions and improving efficiency in traditional, renewable and non-fuel applications.

opex.text: Operating expenses: increased $14.4 million year over year due to higher selling expenses, increased amortization for the acquired intangible assets relating to our QGP acquisition, increased spending on research and development and higher performance-related remuneration accruals .

costs.text: Operating expenses: increased $14.4 million year over year due to higher selling expenses, increased amortization for the acquired intangible assets relating to our QGP acquisition, increased spending on research and development and higher performance-related remuneration accruals .

rd.text: Operating expenses: increased $14.4 million year over year due to higher selling expenses, increased amortization for the acquired intangible assets relating to our QGP acquisition, increased spending on research and development and higher performance-related remuneration accruals .

nonop.heading: Other Income Statement Captions
nonop.text:
Corporate costs: the year over year decrease of $11.0 million was primarily driven by the $8.4 million recovery of historical costs which the Company incurred relating to our defined benefit pension scheme in the U.K., together with a reduction for acquisition related costs, being partly offset by higher information technology investment and the adverse impact of inflationary increases year over year.

Adjustment to fair value of contingent consideration: the charge in 2024 of $3.4 million (2023 - $0.0 million) relates to the accretion of the contingent consideration relating to the acquisition of QGP. See Note 5 of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further information.

Pension scheme settlement charge: the charge in 2024 of $155.6 million (2023 - $0.0 million) relates to the buy-out of our U.K. defined benefit pension scheme. See Note 10 of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further information.

Other net income/(expense): for 2024 and 2023, includes the following:

Interest income/(expense), net: in 2024 was $9.3 million of income, compared to $2.3 million of income in 2023. Interest income from our cash balances has increased due to higher central bank interest rates together with the benefit from our increasing cash balances.

Income taxes: The effective tax rate was 13.6% and 20.2% in 2024 and 2023, respectively.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
We are subject to income and other taxes in the U.S., the U.K., and a number of other jurisdictions. Tax laws are dynamic and subject to change as new laws are passed and new interpretations of the law are issued or applied.

The calculation of our tax liabilities involves evaluating uncertainties in the application of accounting principles and complex tax regulations. We recognize liabilities for anticipated tax audit issues based on our estimate of whether, and the extent to which, additional taxes will be required. If we ultimately determine that payment of these amounts is unnecessary, we reverse the liability and recognize a tax benefit during the period in which we determine that the liability is no longer necessary.

We also recognize tax benefits to the extent that it is more likely than not that our positions will be sustained, based on technical merits of the position, when challenged by the taxing authorities. To the extent that we prevail in matters for which liabilities have been established or are required to pay amounts in excess of the liabilities recorded in our financial statements, our effective tax rate in a given period may be materially affected. An unfavorable tax settlement may require cash payments and result in an increase in our effective tax rate in the year of resolution.

wc.text:

Items excluded from the adjusted working capital calculation are listed in the table below and represent factors which do not fluctuate in line with the day to day working capital needs of the business.

The movements in our adjusted working capital are explained as follows:

We had an $18.1 million decrease in trade and other accounts receivable primarily driven by the timing of sales across our reporting segments and the mix of customer payment terms.

metrics.label: Net margin
metrics.formula: Net income / revenue

metrics.label: Operating cash margin
metrics.formula: Operating cash flow / revenue

metrics.label: Free cash flow margin
metrics.formula: (Operating cash flow − cash CapEx) / revenue

metrics.label: Cash conversion
metrics.formula: Operating cash flow / positive net income

metrics.label: Stock compensation / revenue
metrics.formula: Stock compensation / revenue; not an extra deduction from GAAP earnings

metrics.label: R&D / revenue
metrics.formula: R&D expense / revenue; investment intensity, not a quality verdict

metrics.label: Cash CapEx / revenue
metrics.formula: Cash CapEx / revenue; excludes noncash additions

metrics.label: Accrual ratio
metrics.formula: (Net income − operating cash flow) / average assets; not annualized

metrics.label: Return on average assets
metrics.formula: Net income / average assets; not annualized

metrics.label: Current ratio
metrics.formula: Current assets / current liabilities

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
